chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Hamdan ibn Suleyman from Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Makfouf who said:

I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him) asking him about drinks that are available to us: sikanjabin, julab, mulberry jam, pomegranate jam, quince jam, and apple jam, when the one who sells them is not an expert, and they are sold in our markets. So he wrote: 'It is permissible, there is no problem with them.'
ai.seo_question: Are fruit drinks and jams sold by ordinary vendors permissible in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ja'far ibn Ahmad al-Makfufi queries Imam al-Hassan al-Askari (AS) regarding the permissibility of common fruit-based beverages like sikanjabin and julab sold by non-specialist vendors. The Imam’s concise ruling of 'ja'iz' (permissible) establishes the principle of *al-asl al-suhha* (the default presumption of purity) for commercial goods, indicating that mere lack of religious expertise in the seller does not render the product impure unless specific evidence of adulteration exists. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential approach of relying on general market circulation and common knowledge rather than requiring explicit religious certification for everyday consumables.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahy, from Hamdan Bin Suleyman, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ja’far Bin Ahmad Al Makfouf who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st asking him<sup>asws</sup> about drinking what happens to be facing us, and the ginger drink, and the rose water, and the mulberry jam, and the pomegranate ham, and the quince jam, and the apple jam, when we have bought which is being sold without recognition, and it is being sold in our markets’. So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘Allowed, there is no problem with these’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Hamdan ibn Sulayman from Ali ibn al-Hassan from Ja‘far ibn Ahmad al-Makfuf who has said the following:

“I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, al-Awwal, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about drinks like oxymel, rose- water, jam of mulberry, pomegranate, quince and apple; if the seller is not knowledgeable when they are sold in our market places. He (the Imam) wrote, ‘It is permissible and it is not harmful. 5 ”
